properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 23 at 5:49PM MDT until September 23 at 9:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
Western Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 544 PM MDT, the public reported flooding in the warned area,
with low water crossings along the Rio Hondo inundated with water
and impassable.
- This includes feeder creeks and streams into the Rio Hondo. These
tributaries may inundate additional low water crossings.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tinnie, Hondo, San Patricio and Sunset.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 930 PM MDT THIS EVENING... ...REPLACES FLOOD ADVISORY

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 23 at 1:11PM MDT until September 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, and southeast New
Mexico, including the following areas, in central New Mexico,
Eastern Lincoln County and South Central Mountains. In east central
New Mexico, De Baca County. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves County
Plains and Southwest Chaves County.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rounds of showers and storms will continue through Thursday
night. While rainfall will generally be light to moderate, heavy
rainfall rates up to 2 inches per hour will have the potential to
produce rapid runoff. Soils are becoming increasingly saturated
from persistent rainfall over the past couple of days, further
elevating the risk of flash flooding. Rainfall amounts will
generally range from 1 to 2 inches, with isolated totals up to 4
inches.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, near rivers and streams, and in locations
where the ground is already saturated from recent heavy rainfall.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.  Never drive through flood
waters.  Most flash flood deaths occur in automobiles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE THURSDAY NIGHT
